Create `solution.py` with two functions: `parse_profile(text)` and `profile_is_complete(profile, required_keys)`.

`parse_profile` accepts a string containing zero or more lines. Ignore blank lines and lines whose first non-whitespace character is `#`. Every other line must contain `=` and is split only at its first `=`. Strip surrounding whitespace from both parts. A key must be a nonempty Python-style identifier consisting only of ASCII letters, digits, and underscores and may not begin with a digit. Values may be empty and may contain additional `=` characters. When a key occurs repeatedly, its last value wins. Return a new dictionary. Raise `TypeError` when `text` is not a string and `ValueError` for a malformed active line.

`profile_is_complete` accepts a dictionary and a finite iterable of string keys. It returns `True` exactly when every requested key exists in the dictionary and maps to a nonempty string after stripping whitespace. An empty key iterable returns `True`. Raise `TypeError` if the profile, key iterable, any requested key, or any inspected value has the wrong type. Neither function may mutate or retain aliases to caller-owned containers.

import unittest

from solution import parse_profile, profile_is_complete


class ProfileTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_parse_ignores_comments_and_blanks_and_uses_last_value(self):
        text = """
          # comment = ignored
        name = Ada Lovelace

        token = a=b=c
        empty =
        name= Grace Hopper
        """
        self.assertEqual(parse_profile(text), {
            "name": "Grace Hopper", "token": "a=b=c", "empty": ""
        })

    def test_parse_identifier_boundaries(self):
        self.assertEqual(parse_profile("_x=1\nA9_z = ok"), {"_x": "1", "A9_z": "ok"})
        for line in ("no separator", "=value", "9key=x", "hyphen-key=x", "é=x", "a b=x"):
            with self.subTest(line=line):
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    parse_profile(line)
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            parse_profile(None)

    def test_complete_with_lists_generators_and_empty_iterables(self):
        profile = {"name": " Ada ", "email": "a@example.test", "blank": " \t"}
        self.assertTrue(profile_is_complete(profile, []))
        self.assertTrue(profile_is_complete(profile, (key for key in ["name", "email"])))
        self.assertFalse(profile_is_complete(profile, ["missing"]))
        self.assertFalse(profile_is_complete(profile, ["name", "blank"]))
        self.assertEqual(profile, {"name": " Ada ", "email": "a@example.test", "blank": " \t"})

    def test_complete_type_validation(self):
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            profile_is_complete([], [])
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            profile_is_complete({}, 4)
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            profile_is_complete({"a": "x"}, ["a", 2])
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            profile_is_complete({"a": 12}, ["a"])

    def test_results_do_not_retain_caller_containers(self):
        parsed = parse_profile("x=one")
        parsed["x"] = "changed"
        self.assertEqual(parse_profile("x=one"), {"x": "one"})
        keys = ["x"]
        profile = {"x": "yes"}
        self.assertTrue(profile_is_complete(profile, keys))
        self.assertEqual(keys, ["x"])
        self.assertEqual(profile, {"x": "yes"})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
